judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory notice reciting the TRIA definition of terrorism verbatim; the definition is long but its terms are fixed by federal statute and certification, leaving little for a court to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits beside the war/civil-war exclusion in Crime Exclusion 12(d) and a $0 terrorism premium, so a mild tension exists between 'makes available' coverage and the operative exclusions, but nothing squarely contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain informational recitation of the federal reimbursement formula, with no operative promise and no term needing definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It describes government reimbursement rather than the insurer's obligations, so it does not collide with any operative clause of the Crime section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains the mechanical slip 'ina Program Year', but the meaning is unmistakable and the $100 billion cap is numerically definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Purely a notice of the Treasury cap; it interacts with nothing operative in the General Terms or Crime Coverage Section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite figures and a defined statutory mechanism; 'pro rata allocation in accordance with procedures established by the Secretary' outsources any vagueness to Treasury rules.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It caps liability for certified terrorism losses only, and no other provision of this policy addresses that subject, so no conflict is apparent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single figure of $-0- with no interpretive room whatever.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A zero terrorism premium sits oddly with the notice that terrorism coverage is 'made available', but the Premium Bill and the Crime section give no contrary operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An informational statement about producer compensation with no obligation created and no ambiguous operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses producer compensation, so there is nothing to reconcile it with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear statement that three named coverage sections are claims-made; the named sections are specific and the statement unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 3 of the Declarations shows only General Terms, Crime and Special Coverage were purchased, so this notice describes sections not in this policy — a mismatch, though the notice is expressly aimed at 'prospective insureds'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional and specific ('if a coverage section contains a retroactive date'), with no vague operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No claims-made coverage section is actually attached to this policy, so the prior-acts notice is inert rather than contradictory of anything operative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'claims actually made or incidents reported' is slightly loose, but the claims-made concept it states is standard and self-explanatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime Coverage Section is a discovery-based, not claims-made, form (Exclusion 19 and Subsection 25), so this notice does not govern the coverage actually purchased.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific periods (sixty days automatic, one year optional) tied to named coverage sections; the 'gaps in coverage' language is cautionary, not operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: None of the coverage sections it names were purchased here, and no extended reporting period provision appears in the Crime section, leaving the notice unmatched by any operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely predictive commercial commentary ('substantial annual premium increases'), which creates no right a court would construe, notwithstanding the OCR slip 'matunity'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears no relation to the operative renewal and premium provisions in Subsection 11(g), so no inconsistency arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A capitalised warning using quoted defined terms 'CLAIMS', 'LOSS' and 'DEFENSE COSTS' that are nowhere defined in this policy as issued, which is a real if minor lexical gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It describes limit-eroding defense costs for claims-made sections that were not purchased, while the Crime section's Subsection 25 sets out an entirely different limits structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard consideration preamble subjecting the agreement to the Declarations and other terms; no term is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly subordinates itself to the rest of the policy and thus harmonises rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Coverage shall extend anywhere in the world' is very short and unqualified; its reach against coverage-specific geographic limits is the kind of terse phrase that invites argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime section defines Premises, Banking Premises and In Transit in ways that effectively localise several insuring clauses, so worldwide territory and those definitions must be harmonised, though Subsection 2 gives the coverage section priority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'inconsistent or in conflict with' is a workable standard and the priority rule is stated plainly, giving coverage-section terms control.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the very clause that resolves General Terms/Crime section clashes (e.g. the notice provision in Subsection 5 versus Subsection 27's proof-of-loss conditions), so it is more likely invoked as a tie-breaker than itself found incoherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition; its content is wholly supplied by the applicable coverage section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime Coverage Section defines no term 'Claim' at all, yet the Endorsement 1 late-notice rider and Subsection 5 speak of Claims, leaving a small gap for the purchased coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference with no independent content to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime section does define Insured (Subsection 11), so the referral works cleanly for the purchased coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by pointing to a named item in the Declarations; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 1 of the General Terms Declarations names Medidata Solutions Inc., matching the Crime Declarations Item 1, so the definition is consistent across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite dates by reference to Item 2 and a clear rule for periods other than one year.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 2 as printed shows a garbled 'To 42:01 A.M.' end time, and Endorsement 3 makes discovery 'during the Policy Period' pivotal, so the period's boundaries carry some cross-document weight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain separateness rule for limits and retentions with an express 'unless stated to the contrary' carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Subsection 25 of the Crime section, which does state its own limit and retention rules, exactly as contemplated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed addresses and effective-date rules; the final excuse sentence turns on 'not reasonably possible', a somewhat elastic standard but a familiar one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement/Rider No. 1 adds a prejudice requirement and Crime Subsection 27 imposes a hard ninety-day discovery notice condition precedent, so three notice regimes must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specifies currency, source of exchange rate and the triggering date for each scenario with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Crime Subsection 28 supplies its own valuation and exchange-rate rule keyed to the date of Discovery, but this clause opens with 'Except as otherwise provided in any coverage section', which resolves the overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall do everything necessary' is broad, but standard subrogation language courts apply routinely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection 29 of the Crime section governs distribution of recoveries and dovetails with, rather than contradicts, subrogation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'full compliance with all the terms of this policy' as a condition precedent is broad and has been litigated in other policies, though the clause then spells out the no-action rules concretely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 1(4) permits a direct action by an injured claimant notwithstanding any other provision, which pulls against the no-joinder rule here, and Subsection 27 adds its own suit-limitation period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of agency functions with an exception; the list is closed and each item concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the insuring clauses, which all pay 'the Parent Organization' for loss sustained by an Organization or Client, and with Subsection 27's proof-of-loss duties on the Parent Organization.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An absolute writing-and-signature requirement; the only oddity is the OCR-run 'Nochange', which does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The several endorsements are all signed by an authorized representative, consistent with this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete trigger and a definite twenty-day period; 'at the earliest of the following times' is a clear ordering rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with subparagraphs (b)-(e) as alternatives and with the Policy Period definition in Subsection 3, without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extracted text carries stray OCR fragments '(c) (d) (e) (f)' and page furniture, but the seven enumerated cause grounds are specific and statutory in origin.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The enumerated grounds are exhaustive for post-sixty-day cancellation and sit consistently with (a)'s free cancellation window.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As extracted the clause begins mid-sentence without its '(c)' label, but the substance — insured-initiated termination on prior written notice — is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is one of the enumerated termination routes and does not conflict with the refund rule in (f) or the nonrenewal rules in (g).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'at such other time as may be agreed upon' is open-ended by design; mutual agreement supplies the content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the alteration clause in Subsection 10 requiring written endorsement, though that clause arguably requires a writing this one does not.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite trigger (expiration of the stated Policy Period) with an express cross-reference to paragraph (g).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph (g) does exist and supplies the nonrenewal notice machinery, so the cross-reference is sound.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'customary short rates' is an industry term left undefined in the policy, which is a genuine if narrow lexical gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Subsection 11's termination routes and nothing else in the policy addresses premium refunds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very long but highly specified: day counts, rate comparisons and lettered scenarios leave little to construe, though 'incomplete or late' notice is somewhat open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph (iii) increases aggregate limits pro rata for extensions, which must be read with the Crime section's per-loss limits in Subsection 25, but no contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple mailing obligation with a definite addressee and address standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the notice provisions in Subsection 5 and with (i)'s content requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence content requirement, definite on its face; in the policy text it runs into the next heading, but the extracted provision is clean.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements (b) and (g) without altering them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: the bonds identified in Item 4 terminate at inception, with no vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 4 names policy 8212-1392 for the prior year — the same number as this policy — and Subsection 24 (Liability for Prior Losses) plus Endorsement 3's deletion of it complicate what happens to that prior coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, symmetric statement of the effect of insolvency; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses bankruptcy, so there is nothing to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard headings-are-not-operative clause, plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated in every endorsement, so it is consistent throughout the instrument, even though many provisions are cross-referenced by their headings (e.g. 'Subsection 22 Legal Expenses Extension').

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extracted text carries orphan numerals '(1) (2) (3) (4)', and 'prejudiced the Company' is a standard but fact-laden notion; the rule itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the notice provisions in Subsection 5 and, arguably, the ninety-day and six-month conditions precedent in Crime Subsection 27, which are not framed as Claim reporting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'not reasonably possible' and 'as soon as reasonably possible' are elastic, but they are settled New York statutory formulations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates almost verbatim the final paragraph of General Terms Subsection 5, so the two are consistent rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Burden allocation is precise by date, and the irrebuttable presumption grounds are two specific events.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a defined 'Claim', which the Crime Coverage Section does not define, but the rider is aimed at liability sections generally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short savings clause; 'to duplicate coverage under multiple policy periods' is terse but its purpose is evident.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the claims-made timing provisions, which matters little here since the purchased Crime section is discovery-based.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'death or personal injury, as that term is defined by the New York Insurance Law' imports an external definition, and the extracted text includes page furniture mid-sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the claimant may sue directly 'notwithstanding any other provision', which pulls directly against the no-action/no-joinder rule in General Terms Subsection 8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate headings and 'all other terms remain unchanged'; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Standard in every endorsement here; the phrase only matters where two endorsements amend the same clause, which is not the case for this rider.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'trade or economic sanctions or other similar laws or regulations' is a general catch-all appended to specific categories, and 'to the extent that' leaves the reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the worldwide territory grant in Subsection 1 without expressly saying so, though the two can be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure boilerplate about headings and unchanged terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the identical clause in the other endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A consideration preamble expressly subject to the Declarations and General Terms; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It confirms the layering that Subsection 2 of the General Terms establishes, so it harmonises the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'direct loss' is the operative limiter and has generated litigation generally, but here Theft, Forgery and Employee are all defined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is amended for ERISA Plans by Subsection 21(a) and narrowed by Exclusions 12(c), 12(n) and 13, all of which cross-reference it coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A layered clause with lettered and roman-numeraled sub-parts; the trailing qualifier 'committed by a Third Party' sits after a list, leaving some doubt whether it modifies items (i)-(iv) or all of them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 14 removes Forgery, Computer Fraud and Funds Transfer Fraud from this clause and Exclusion 15 removes extortion payments, so its boundaries are set elsewhere but consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same structure as Insuring Clause 2, with a dangling 'committed by a Third Party' after two sub-items and the odd phrase 'within the home of an Employee or an Organization'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with the In Transit definition and Exclusions 14 and 15, which expressly carve out mail, carriers and extortion, without contradiction.
